frameworks.name: Consumer-Feels-Like-Robbing-You Offer Design
frameworks.definition: Bundle near-zero-COGS digital assets (PDF guides, private social access) onto a physical product so the perceived value overwhelms the price point, making the tangible product feel like a bonus rather than the core purchase.

claims.text: Greg Short and Mari bundled near-zero-marginal-cost digital assets (instant-download PDF workout guides, access to a private Instagram page with workout footage, and access to a private Facebook community) with a $19.99 physical booty band, making the physical product feel like a secondary bonus. Only the physical band carried meaningful COGS; all digital components cost only time to create. Over a two-to-three-year period this offer structure produced over one million units sold.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: physical consumer product with low per-unit COGS
digital assets deliverable at near-zero marginal cost (PDF, private social groups)
claims.mechanism: When digital bonuses overwhelm the perceived value of the physical product, the buyer experiences the price as a bargain relative to the totality of what they receive, raising purchase intent and reducing price resistance.

numbers.axis: units sold over the offer's lifetime

bounded_by: Requires that digital assets be genuinely useful and contextually relevant to the physical product (not arbitrary filler)
Physical product must still carry real value; the strategy collapses if the core item is low-quality

claims.text: Greg Short asserts that in a competitive physical-product market, winning requires creating an offer so dense with value that the consumer perceives the price as a steal relative to alternatives, making every competing product offering appear obsolete by comparison.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
claims.speaker_term: so much value that you disrupt and you make everyone else's product offering completely obsolete
conditions: B2C physical product category where commoditization pressure is high
consumer price point where digital bonuses can meaningfully shift perceived value
claims.mechanism: Competitors who sell only the physical item cannot match the total value bundle without incurring proportional cost increases, because the seller's digital bonuses have near-zero marginal cost to replicate.
bounded_by: Does not apply if the buyer is sophisticated and evaluates only the core product (e.g., professional equipment buyers who strip bonuses from the price)

claims.text: Greg Short and Mari's offer bundled access to private Instagram pages and private Facebook communities alongside a physical product purchase, creating ongoing engagement touchpoints at zero marginal cost to the seller after initial setup.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: physical product category with a natural affinity community (fitness, hobby, wellness)
seller already active on relevant social platforms
claims.mechanism: Private community access creates post-purchase value that is not consumed at the moment of sale, giving buyers a reason to remain engaged with the brand and driving word-of-mouth referrals from within the community.
bounded_by: Requires that the community be actively maintained with relevant content; inactive communities erode perceived value and damage brand trust

claims.text: Greg Short's booty band offer achieved high gross margins because only the physical band carried hard COGS; the PDF guides, private Instagram access, and private Facebook community added substantial consumer-facing value at effectively zero additional per-unit cost.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: physical product bundled with digital/community bonuses
seller has existing social media presence capable of hosting private groups
claims.mechanism: Digital bonuses (PDFs, private social channels) have zero marginal replication cost after initial creation, so adding them to a physical product bundle expands perceived value without expanding COGS, expanding gross margin per unit.
bounded_by: Seller must invest time upfront to create the digital assets; this is a fixed cost that amortizes over unit volume

examples.text: Greg Short and his business partner Mari sold over one million booty bands at $19.99 each over a two-to-three-year period. To win against commodity competitors, they attached instant-download PDF workout guides, access to a private Instagram page with workout footage and form instruction, and access to a private Facebook community to every purchase. The result: consumers were so excited about the totality of the bundle that the physical band became secondary in their perception. Only the band itself had meaningful COGS; all digital components cost only creation time to deliver. The consumer felt they were getting an outsized deal, and the offer converted at scale.

practices.text: When designing a physical product offer, attach instant-access digital bonuses (PDF guides, private social communities, instructional content) whose perceived value exceeds the price of the physical product, so the buyer feels they are getting the digital suite for free and the tangible item as a bonus.

Identify all components of your offer that have zero or near-zero marginal cost to deliver (digital downloads, community access, instructional videos) and bundle them prominently so customers attribute the bulk of the value to items that cost you nothing to replicate.
